methodology.purpose: Qualitative context for Stage 1 qualifiers only; no final prop selection.
methodology.evidence_policy: Separate facts from interpretation; do not equate fantasy points allowed with receiving yards/receptions allowed.
methodology.odds: DraftKings lines/prices carried from Stage 1 snapshot; not independently live-verified.

injury_notes: WAS C Lucas Patrick ruled out; Nick Allegretti expected to start.
Jayden Daniels full participation; no game designation in official report.
Chig Okonkwo full participation Tuesday after Monday limited.
Treylon Burks Monday DNP, Tuesday limited; secondary report expects him to play, final official designation not confirmed.
J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo full participation Tuesday; no injury designations Wednesday.
Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Theo Johnson full participation.
Terry McLaurin listed out by secondary matchup report.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice; 1,250 passing yards/7 TDs. WAS averages 207.1 pass yds/game.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG pass defense ranks 3rd (177.8 allowed/game); starting C Lucas Patrick ruled out; Allegretti expected to start.
assessments.interpretation: Health and baseline volume are positive, but a strong pass defense and OL change temper the outlook.

assessments.supporting_evidence: No injury designation after full practice; led NYG with 98 carries/418 yards through Week 9 and 58% of RB carries+targets.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Missed previous game with hamstring injury; WAS rush defense ranks 12th (102.3 allowed/game); no DK rushing market row in snapshot.
assessments.interpretation: Lead-back role is strong if workload returns, but post-injury workload is uncertain and no DK line is available.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Next-largest NYG backfield workload behind Skattebo.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Skattebo cleared and held 58% of RB carries+targets vs Singletary 27%; WAS ranks 12th in rush defense.
assessments.interpretation: Return of primary back reduces Singletary's expected touch share.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Jacory Croskey-Merritt out; White has 54 carries at 4.2 YPC through Week 9.
assessments.contrary_evidence: White and Ekeler split workload; Week 9 White 7 carries/28 yards, Ekeler 8/16. NYG rush D ranks 21st (123.6 allowed).
assessments.interpretation: Favorable matchup and absence of Croskey-Merritt help, but Ekeler remains a meaningful competitor.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 78 targets, 53 catches, 648 yards; 30% NYG target share; full practice and no designation.
assessments.contrary_evidence: WAS pass defense ranks 30th, allowing 240 yards/game; team-level measure, not receiver-specific.
assessments.interpretation: Target concentration, cleared health and opponent passing profile support the opportunity.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 78 targets and 53 catches; about 30% target share; full practice.
assessments.contrary_evidence: WAS allows 240 pass yards/game, 30th-ranked pass defense; not a direct receptions-allowed metric.
assessments.interpretation: Strong target share provides a solid catch-volume foundation.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice and no game designation after chest issue.
assessments.contrary_evidence: 26 targets, 12 catches, 167 yards; about 9% target share; behind Nabers, Fields and Likely in target hierarchy.
assessments.interpretation: Availability is positive, but season-long opportunity is modest.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Cleared for game with full practice.
assessments.contrary_evidence: 12 catches on 26 targets; competing targets from Nabers, Fields and Likely.
assessments.interpretation: Low threshold helps, but limited target volume creates a fragile floor.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 30 catches/303 yards/5 TD on 49 targets; McLaurin out, leaving Diggs a principal option.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG pass defense ranks 3rd (177.8 allowed/game); Diggs target share down ~3 percentage points over recent three-game sample.
assessments.interpretation: Leading role is positive, but strong defense and declining recent share temper outlook.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 30 receptions on 49 targets; 19.8% target share; McLaurin out.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG pass defense ranks 3rd; recent target share down ~3 percentage points.
assessments.interpretation: Meaningful role supports catches, but matchup and recent trend make the signal mixed.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Usage source reports recent snap/target-share growth; secondary report expects him to play.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Foot: Monday DNP, Tuesday limited; final official designation not confirmed; only 12 catches on 22 targets through Week 9.
assessments.interpretation: Role trend is encouraging but health and workload remain uncertain.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Week 9: 36 snaps (58%) and 7 targets; McLaurin out.
assessments.contrary_evidence: Seven targets is a one-game spike; stable multi-week role and season-level totals not verified.
assessments.interpretation: Low line plus recent opportunity is promising, but depends heavily on one game.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Week 9: 7 targets, 20.6% of team targets; 58% snap share.
assessments.contrary_evidence: One-game spike; season-level catch volume not verified.
assessments.interpretation: Recent role is encouraging but volatility is high.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 69 targets, 46 catches, 448 yards; 26.5% target share; 75% snap share.
assessments.contrary_evidence: WAS allows third-most fantasy points/game to TEs; Likely recent target share down ~5 points.
assessments.interpretation: Substantial involvement and favorable TE matchup outweigh modest recent share decline.

assessments.supporting_evidence: 69 targets/46 catches; 26.5% target share; favorable TE matchup vs WAS (third-most fantasy points allowed).
assessments.contrary_evidence: Recent target share down ~5 percentage points.
assessments.interpretation: Target base and positional matchup support catch volume, though involvement has cooled.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice and no game designation.
assessments.contrary_evidence: 136 NYG snaps (~24%) vs Likely's 420 (75%); insufficient current target-volume evidence.
assessments.interpretation: Healthy but appears behind Likely in TE role; limited demonstrated opportunity.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice and no game designation.
assessments.contrary_evidence: 136 snaps vs Likely's 420; no verified target-volume evidence to support a dependable catch workload.
assessments.interpretation: Role hierarchy is the primary concern.

assessments.supporting_evidence: Full practice Tuesday after Monday limited; 31 targets/23 catches/238 yards; 19% target share; Week 9: 7 targets.
assessments.contrary_evidence: NYG pass defense ranks 3rd (177.8 allowed/game); season totals span only six games.
assessments.interpretation: Recent target volume and playing time are positive, but matchup and small sample temper confidence.

sources.title: McCarthy and Skattebo no injury designations

caveats: Usage/snap figures are third-party compiled, not official NFL stat feeds.
Team pass defense rank is not direct coverage/receptions allowed.
TE fantasy points allowed is not directly equivalent to receiving yards or catches allowed.
Van Jefferson Week 9 seven-target game is a one-game sample.
Treylon Burks final game status remains unconfirmed in official injury source.
No DK rushing line for Cam Skattebo in the Stage 1 snapshot.
